messages:
maya: CI microbench failed on PR-9234, tail latency jump on kv-cache workload. blocking merge until we understand cause

sam: saw same in local CI reproducer. p99 went from ~28ms to ~240ms on a 4k sequence run. p50 unchanged. looks like a small fraction of requests get stuck in scheduler.

ci-bot: [CI] microbench/kvcache-x86-64: threshold diff exceeded (p99: +212ms) — https://ci.redwood.example/runs/7821

liam: assigning myself to bisect. suspect kernel-affinity tweak from yesterday's batcher refactor.

sam: steps i ran: 
```
# reproduce
bazel test //perf:kvcache_micro --test_output=all --runs=30
# profile one of the slow runs
perf record -g -o perf.data -- ./bazel-bin/perf/kvcache_micro --run-id=12
perf script | flamegraph.pl > slow-flame.svg
```

nora: attached the failing perf output from CI run: histogram p50=26ms p95=42ms p99=248ms mean=34ms. 3 samples at ~5s each. logs show "wait_for_batch: queued 1->0 after 5004ms" twice.

maya: thanks. those 5s stalls smell like a scheduling wakeup edgecase. could be the new atomic spin->sleep path introduced in commit abc123.

liam: bisect results: bad commit is abc123 (author: liam) — changeset: 
```
commit abc123
Author: liam
Date: 2026-02-10
- change: batch_scheduler: prefer_cpu_affinity_on_small_batches()
- change: add sleep_path_on_low_load()
```

sam: interesting, the change was intended to reduce power and polyfill GPU affinity heuristics. but the sleep_path_on_low_load() uses a condition variable with a 5s fallback to avoid livelock — i think that's the 5s we see.

liam: looking at code: the fallback path uses `cv.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::milliseconds(5000))` inside the low-load branch, which is only supposed to be taken if the CPU has no work for several attempts. but race with `enqueue()` can leave thread sleeping until timeout if notify is missed.

nora: reproduced a missed-notify locally by adding a tight timing window: inserted `std::this_thread::yield()` between enqueue and notify and saw same p99 spike.

sam: proposal: change to `cv.wait_for` loop with predicate or use sem_post-style wake semantics; or just revert abc123 for CI hotfix.

maya: can we do a scoped revert PR to unblock rollout? we should also add a microbench test that exercises the specific notify race.

liam: opened PR-9240: revert abc123 (small revert, drops affinity & sleep_path). CI run queued. link: https://git.redwood.internal/p/9240

ci-bot: PR-9240 build: all tests queued. running microbench suite now.

nora: after revert applied to a local build, ran repro 50 times: p99 stable ~30ms, no 5s samples. good sign.

sam: adding a unit test: `BatcherNotifyRaceTest` that injects a delayed-notify path and asserts no sample > 1s across 1000 iterations. will push to next patch.

maya: timeline: revert merge to unstick release, follow up with durable fix that uses eventfd on linux (no missed-notify). create follow-up RFC.

liam: note for postmortem: tests didn't cover the edge timing path. also CI microbench threshold should include a small test that runs tight enqueue/dequeue at low load to catch this.

maya: thanks all. reassigning to eng-oncall to monitor after revert. will redeploy canary tomorrow morning and watch p99. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: [CI] PR-9240 microbench run: p99 delta -0.1ms (regression cleared).

sam: great. opening follow-up PR with eventfd-based notifier and new unit test.

nora: adding perf profile snippet to the PR description to help reviewers.

maya: closing thread, move to postmortem + tests.
